To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the structure of TTR Y78 F reveals a destabilization of contacts in the AB loop, and the structure of T TR R104H reveals new contacts involving the amino-terminal region and His 104.
the Y78F mutation destabilizes the contacts between the AB loop and the rest of the molecule and that the R104H mutation creates a new contact involving the N-terminal and the C-terminal regions.

the structure of TTR Y78, a mutant associated with amyloid formation, reveals destabilization of the alpha-helix/AB loop region and the N-terminal region of the molecule, whereas in the TTR variant R104H, the N-terminal region is stabilized by the introduction of a new salt bridge involving the side chain of His104.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the elucidation of the three-dimensional structure and molecular basis of two important TRT variants, Y78F and R104H, and the molecular basis for their respective amyloidogenic and protective nature.
understanding the molecular basis for the amyloidogenic process, and the results presented here provide new insights into the molecular mechanisms of TTR amyloidogenesis.
the structural bases for the amyloidogenic and non-amyloidogenic properties of TTR variants.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
TTR Y78 is a destabilizing mutation and TTR R 104H is a stabilizing mutation.

the TTR Y78 mutation destabilizes the tetrameric structure of the molecule by weakening the interactions between the N-terminal domain and the AB loop and the beta-sheet region, whereas the R104H mutation strengthens the tetrameric interactions by introducing new contacts between the N-terminal region, helix A, and the beta-sheet.
TTR R104 protects against amyloid formation by a mechanism that involves the formation of new contacts that stabilize the protein tetramer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, in the case of TTR Y78, a destabilization of a set of interdomain contacts is observed, and in the case of the TTR R 104H variant, new interdomain contacts are formed, both of which are related to the amyloidoses.
, by means of X-ray crystallographic techniques, we have identified the molecular basis of two important TTr variants.
the Y78F mutation destabilizes the protein structure, and the R104H mutation stabilizes the protein structure.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the amyloidogenic process can be explained in terms of destabilization of the protein molecule, which is the result of a set or combination of different structural alterations, some of which are more significant than others.
a detailed knowledge of the structural features of TTR variants is crucial to understanding amyloid formation and the development of new therapies for amyloidosis.
a subtle change in the protein structure may lead to the amyloid fibril formation, and that the structural basis for amyloidogenesis is not necessarily the same for all mutations.
